articles.title: Marching bands raise hundreds of thousands to keep their Macy's parade dreams alive
articles.summary: The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade will go ahead Saturday after being postponed earlier this week for the first time in its history. The lineup was announced this month, but the participation of some performers was thrown into doubt when a fierce nor'easter forced the parade to be delayed . The parade's executive producer, Will Coss, said on Thursday that there had been an "overwhelmingly positive response" from the performers as organizers tried to resolve issues. "We're actively working through all the pieces of our parade, but I have to say there's an overwhelming positive response," he told TODAY. "Our performers, our talent, our performance groups, our bands… we're all coming together to try to figure this out. We're optimistic we're going to have a really successful parade on Saturday morning." What marching bands are set to perform? Several bands have scrambled to stay in New York for the rescheduled parade, with some raising money for their extended stay in a matter of hours. The Pride of Pearland band from Texas raised an extra $350,000 in under 24 hours to extend its stay. "Because of YOU, the Pride of Pearland Band & Color Guard has met our fundraising goal to cover the unexpected costs of extra days in New York City," it posted on Instagram. "To everyone who donated, shared our story, made a call or sent encouragement—THANK YOU. You helped make it possible for our 500+ students to stay and experience the moment they've worked so hard for. View this post on Instagram Elsewhere, the Concord Community High School Marching Minutemen from Elkhart, Ind., were already planning to be in the New York area through Saturday, so their plans are unaffected. Dobyns-Bennett High School from Kingsport, Tenn., is reported to have secured the extra funding it needed, as has James F. Byrnes High School from Duncan, S.C., which met its funding goal. The University of Illinois Marching Illini are also staying, after launching a fundraiser to cover an extra $175,000 in costs. The Nā Koa Aliʻi Hawaiʻi All-State band is staying too, with the band telling Hawaii News Now it has raised $500,000 of the $700,000 it needs to cover its costs so far. The Na Koa Ali'l HI All State Marching Band have raised $500,000 to stay for the parade. Eugene Gologursky via Getty Images The University of Connecticut band is also staying, and said it will make its first-ever appearance at the parade thanks to generous donors. Not everyone can stay, though, with the University of Alabama's Million Dollar Band returning to Tuscaloosa for the Iron Bowl, which kicks off at 6:30 p.m. Saturday. Macy's Great American Marching Band is also unable to take part, according to NBC , after they couldn't make the new date work financially. Individual performers have been affected as well. Cheerleader Lola Smith of Phoenix is staying to perform with Spirit of America cheer, but other members of the Mesa, Ariz. group are not, AZ Family reported. Who are the headline acts? Megan Moroney captured during rehearsals on Nov. 24. (Photo by Manny Carabel/Getty Images) Manny Carabel via Getty Images According to the list of performers on broadcast partner NBC's website , Grammy-nominated acts RAYE, Teddy Swims and country singer Megan Moroney are set to perform. Other headliners include Queen Latifah, Keke Palmer, Jimmy Fallon & The Roots and JoJo. The wider line-up includes EJAE, Indigo Girls, Natalie Merchant, Baha Men, Natasha Bedingfield, Blues Traveler, DEVO, Feid, Icona Pop, Il Volo, Wyclef Jean, Jamie Miller, RIIZE and Smash Mouth. There is also a tribute to the late Queen of country, Dolly Parton, led by Megan Hilty. Broadway stars Leslie Odom Jr. and Anthony Ramos are also performing, as is Hunger Games actor Mckenna Grace. Special appearances are said to be planned from Jack McBrayer, Janet McTeer, John Stamos, Melissa Joan Hart, as well as Holly Robinson Peete and Rodney Peete. The all-star Broadway medley is going ahead, according to Deadline , with performers from The Lost Boys, The Rocky Horror Show, Wicked, Schmigadoon!, Aladdin, The Book of Mormon and Chicago confirmed. Paddington the Musical will appear on a separate float. Macy's has not yet confirmed that every act can make the new date. What time is it due to start? The parade steps off at 8:30 a.m. ET Saturday and is broadcast on NBC, Peacock and Telemundo. The 2.5-mile route runs from the Upper West Side down to Macy's Herald Square flagship store at 34th Street and Seventh Avenue. It usually wraps up by noon. NBC will also air an encore presentation at 2 p.m. This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/article/the-macys-thanksgiving-day-parade-is-on-for-saturday-one-high-school-band-had-to-scramble-an-extra-350000-to-make-it-141710254.html

articles.title: More than 400,000 still without power after Thanksgiving storms batter both coasts
articles.summary: A Thanksgiving storm brought foul weather to the East Coast and Midwest on Thursday, causing major power outages , disrupting holiday travel and prompting the historic postponement of New York City's Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade. More than 440,000 customers were without power Friday afternoon across the Midwest and Northeast, according to the utility tracking website PowerOutage.us . Of those, more than 109,000 customers were without electricity in Pennsylvania, along with more than 68,000 in New Jersey and 54,000 in Maryland. The outages reached more than 800,000 customers at the height of the storm Thursday night. There were 2,286 flights in the U.S. delayed as of Friday afternoon, with another 137 canceled, according to the flight tracking service FlightAware . That nearly equals the 2,500 flights to or from U.S. destinations delayed on Thursday, though more than 460 were canceled, according to FlightAware. The storm hammered sections of the East Coast with torrential rain, high winds and flooding. All of New Jersey was under a state of emergency , declared by Gov. Mikie Sherrill on Wednesday night, as were parts of New York , following a declaration from Gov. Kathy Hochul. The weather service posted wind advisories from northern Georgia to most of the mid-Atlantic to southern New England. Stormy weather creates havoc in New York City New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Thursday morning that two people had to be rescued from their cars because of flooding. He cautioned people not to attempt to walk, bike or drive through flooded areas. "We want to remind everyone to stay safe and there is no destination worth your safety," Mamdani said. The New York City Emergency Management agency reported that the city received 1.5 to 2 inches of rain on Thanksgiving, with some parts seeing up to 3 inches. High tides brought flooding to the city's coastal areas, including portions of Staten Island and Long Island. Central Park saw wind gusts higher than 30 mph, the agency said, while LaGuardia Airport recorded winds of 56 mph. Several scaffolding structures collapsed in the wind, with no injuries were reported. Macy's postponed the annual Thanksgiving parade until Saturday because of concerns about how the parade's massive balloons would fare in the wind-swept canyons between Manhattan's skyscrapers. A high school marching band from Pearland, Texas, near Houston, said it raised a staggering $350,000 to allow its 500 members to stay in New York City for two extra nights. "This was quite a challenge for us, and there was a very frantic and large call to action to our community to let the kids stay here and finish it out," Ryan Demkovich, the director of the Pride of Pearland Marching Band for Pearland High School, told CBS News on Thursday. Visitors who had traveled to New York to attend the parade were forced to make last-minute changes to their travel plans. Amanda Anderson, a Florida-based makeup artist who was hired to do makeup for parade performers, told CBS News New York she was able to rebook her flights so she could stay an extra day. "I was in Macy's, actually, when I found out, and I look up and there was like three girls crying already," Anderson said when she learned the parade had been postponed. "People were sitting down, very somber. It was an experience." Major roadways flooded, holiday travel disrupted The storm flooded coastal villages and cities from North Carolina through New Jersey as the high tide rolled in Thursday morning. Roads were closed and emergency workers were rescuing people from cars stranded in water. Avalon, New Jersey, was seeing some of the worst flooding in its history, Borough of Avalon Business Administrator Scott J. Wahl said. "Not quite Hurricane Sandy," Wahl said of the benchmark storm for his village on the far south of New Jersey's Atlantic coast. Floodwaters washed debris over the road next to the shore, and a few drivers had to be rescued after driving around barricades and into floodwaters, but no injuries were reported, Wahl said. Lance Miller, 54, said floods in his neighborhood of Ocean City, a small coastal town in New Jersey, are about a foot deep and that driving to the nearest grocery store would probably "destroy your car." "I wouldn't do that, I'm a car guy," said Miller. "You're gonna have a good foot of water that you'd have to drive through." Miller, who had his Thanksgiving Day meal preparations set, said he would be staying indoors and have dinner with his wife and daughter. But he said some of his friends in the area were "not so lucky" and had flooding inside their homes. "So they're dealing with cleanup, you know," he said. The Margate City Fire Department near Atlantic City, New Jersey, posted a video on Facebook of water pouring through the city's streets on a gray day even before heavy rains started. A firefighter there said the tide was coming in ferociously and it was still an hour before its peak. Water closed in on steps to houses, and businesses had sandbags piled in front of their doors. A stretch of U.S. Route 30, a major artery that goes into Atlantic City, was shuttered in both directions due to heavy flooding, the Absecon Police Department reported. "Please stay off the roads until conditions improve," Absecon police said. "Do not attempt to drive through flooded roadways or around barricades." Chester County Hospital in West Chester, Pennsylvania, sustained a partial power outage on Thursday afternoon, but power was restored before patients had to be transported to other facilities. Residents of the Pennsylvania community of Springfield Township north of Philadelphia were asked to temporarily evacuate out of caution after a tree fell on a propane tank, local officials said. That evacuation advisory was later lifted. The storm prompted the temporary closure of some coastal highways and bridges. The nearly 18-mile Chesapeake Bay Bridge-Tunnel over the Chesapeake Bay in Virginia was closed for several hours Thursday morning because of high winds, while NC 12, the only highway connecting Hatteras Island on the North Carolina Outer Banks to the mainland, was closed after seawater breached the dunes again and covered the two-lane highway. North Carolina was particularly hard-hit by heavy rain. Emerald Isle, in the state's Outer Banks, received 9.16 inches of rain. Atlantic Beach, North Carolina, saw 9.06 inches. In Maryland, nearly 2 million water customers in Montgomery and Prince George's counties, which are in the Washington metropolitan area, were asked to conserve water by the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission      because of intermittent power disruptions associated with the storm. The water conservation request, which applied to all 1.9 million WSSC customers, was due to the risk that power outages posed to the agency's two water filtration plants. Heavy snow fell on parts of Illinois and Missouri with St. Louis recording 7.3 inches of snowfall. French Village, Missouri, received 15 inches of show while Ste. Genevieve recorded 14 inches. The ice arena in Wentzville, Missouri, which hosts hockey and other ice skating activities, was empty when the roof caved in at about 3 a.m., according to the city. The rain isn't quite over yet for the Northeast. More storms are expected Sunday night into Monday morning for New York City, Philadelphia and Boston. articles.title: Hackers breach U.S. Air Force's flagship cloud computing platform
articles.summary: (Corrects date to 2026 in paragraph 7) By Mike Stone and Raphael Satter WASHINGTON, Nov 27 (Reuters) - Hackers have breached the US Air Force's flagship cloud computing platform, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters, in a development that could jeopardize a vast swathe of sensitive tactical, ‌personnel and logistics data. The intrusion at Cloud One was discovered within the past month or so during work to upgrade the system, two of ‌the people said, adding that the discovery has led to disruption across the platform. Reuters could not establish the identity of the hackers, the full scope of the intrusion or whether any data ​had been stolen. In a statement to Reuters, the Air Force said it "does not comment on the security posture, vulnerabilities or operational status of specific networks and systems. We continuously take prudent measures to protect Department (of the Air Force) information, systems and mission capabilities." A ONE-STOP SHOP Initiated in 2017, Cloud One was meant to serve as a one-stop shop for the Air Force's IT needs, combining the resources of four operators — Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle and Alphabet — to power scores of applications including ones that manage personnel data and pay ‌or logistics and maintenance. Among them are the Air Force's Cloud-Based ⁠Command and Control, which collates air defense radar and other data feeds from across North America, and the Theater Integrated Combat Munitions System, which tracks bombs and missiles across more than 200 US Air Force locations around the world. SAIC was the prime ⁠contractor for Cloud One until 2026, when Leidos took over. SAIC did not respond to a request seeking comment. Leidos referred questions to the Air Force. Cloud One is among the US military's biggest cloud platforms, according to two of the sources. "A breach here is a big deal," one of the sources said. Investigators have called in Cyber Command, the US military's cyber force, ​to ​assess the damage, one of the sources said. Cyber Command did not respond to requests for ​comment. A RANGE OF DISRUPTION The discovery of the hack led to a ‌range of disruption. Two of the sources, along with a fourth person familiar with the matter, said that efforts to migrate back-office applications to Cloud One, a longstanding military priority, have been paused. Updates to applications already running on Cloud One were blocked, leaving Air Force personnel unable to apply fixes just as a new batch of serious software vulnerabilities has been disclosed across the technology industry. A fifth source said that some users had their administrator rights revoked. All five sources spoke on condition of anonymity. One source said that the cyber intruders exploited a software vulnerability to reach the control plane. That person likened the control plane to a universal remote, ‌as intruders in theory could leverage their access to check the operational status of military aircraft ​or the movement of spare parts, though it was unclear whether the hackers did so in ​this case. Reuters could not identify the specific vulnerability exploited by the hackers. STRING ​OF HACKS News of the breach comes amid heightened anxiety over AI-powered intrusions, a particularly serious problem for cloud-based networks because of the ‌ability of AI models to swiftly detect weaknesses across wide ​surface areas. The US government already has been dealing ​with the fallout from at least six other recently disclosed cyber incidents, including two at the FBI, a previous hack of Pentagon data, a recent leak of Department of Homeland Security personnel information, a breach affecting at least two spy agencies and a hack at the Treasury Department. Cloud One has long ​been in the crosshairs of hackers. In a 2023 commentary ‌carried by the online publication FedScoop, Cloud One's leadership touted what they called a "100% success rate" in beating back what they said was ​a "staggering" number of attempts to penetrate the platform. "There is no room for error when it comes to security," Cloud One's leadership wrote. (Reporting by ​Mike Stone and Raphael Satter in Washington; Editing by Chris Sanders and Will Dunham) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/exclusive-hackers-breach-us-air-110252874.html

articles.title: U.S. opens hotline for tips about cartels, angering Mexico
articles.summary: Mexico's president has blasted the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration after it set up anonymous tip lines in the country, accusing American officials of "interference" and not doing enough to fight fentanyl and corruption inside their own borders. President Claudia Sheinbaum said Friday the country's foreign ministry has lodged a formal complaint with U.S. Ambassador Ron Johnson. "We have made it very clear in our relationship with the United States that the relationship is one of coordination, not subordination," she said in her daily news briefing. Sheinbaum, in harsh comments Thursday, read excerpts from a new investigation by The Associated Press revealing how the DEA allowed at least 1.4 million counterfeit fentanyl pills to go unseized as it spent eight months tracking a drug trafficking ring flooding the Southwest with deadly drugs. "The DEA has plenty of work to do in its own country. A lot," Sheinbaum said, pointing to the AP report. "The first thing it should do is investigate corruption in the United States linked to organized crime, or what they call terrorist groups." "It's clearly an act of interference," Sheinbaum added. Imagine, she mused, if Mexico "opened a WhatsApp service for reporting corruption in the United States. How would the U.S. government view that?" Sheinbaum's angry response comes less than 24 hours after DEA Administrator Terry Cole announced the tip lines on his X account, encouraging Mexicans to denounce members of criminal networks in Sinaloa state, the corrupt officials who support them and people who launder money to finance narcoterrorism. "Your information matters. Your identity and your safety matter," Cole said, specifying that tips submitted via Signal, WhatsApp and email would be handled confidentially. U.S. steps up pressure on Mexico The United States has stepped up pressure on Mexico to fight the cartels and has even offered to deploy troops on Mexican soil, something Sheinbaum has ruled out while maintaining that there will be security cooperation with Washington, "but without subordination." On Nov. 20, Mexican military forces captured drug lord Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, alias "El Chapo Isidro," a key ally of a Sinaloa cartel faction. The FBI had placed him on its list of 10 most wanted fugitives , while the U.S. State Department offered a reward of up to $5 million for information leading to his arrest. The military operation o capture him tsparked panic in the region, sending civilians fleeing from erupting gunfire. Elsewhere in the state, suspected gang members reportedly erected improvised roadblocks. In clashes with security forces , 16 cartel suspects were killed, officials said, and four soldiers also died. Mexico requested Washington's support for the operation, and the United States sent a drone to help gather information about the drug lord's whereabouts. The U.S. has requested Meza Flores' extradition, but Mexican Attorney General Ernestina Godoy said he will be tried in Mexico. Chapo Isidro's capture came just days after Sheinbaum met President Trump on the sidelines of a summit in Asia. Mr. Trump, who has pushed Mexico to do more to tackle drug gangs, said Friday that the two had discussed trade and security. The Mexican government has knocked out several cartel kingpins. Chief among them was Mexico's most powerful cartel leader , known as "El Mencho ," who was killed in February. Similar to the capture of Meza Flores, the dramatic operation resulted in a burst of violence and burning cars. Although cooperation between the two countries went smoothly in that operation, tensions arose between Mexico and Washington in late April after federal prosecutors in New York made public a drug trafficking indictment against Sinaloa Gov. Rubén Rocha Moya , a member of Mexico's governing party. He and nine other officials were accused of collaborating with a faction of the Sinaloa cartel, which the Trump administration has designated a foreign terrorist organization. Amid the controversy, Rocha Moya took an indefinite leave of absence, and his bank accounts in Mexico were frozen. But Mexican authorities refused to carry out the U.S. request to arrest him. Former Sinaloa Security Secretary Gerardo Mérida Sánchez surrendered to U.S. authorities in May. DEA accused of "walking" fentanyl DEA whistleblowers in June revealed to the AP how agents in New Mexico in recent years permitted hundreds of thousands of fentanyl pills to go unseized. At the time, the DEA denied it ever knowingly allowed the trafficking of a synthetic opioid the White House has designated a "weapon of mass destruction." That denial, however, was further contradicted by new AP findings that the DEA permitted at least 1.4 million additional pills to be trafficked between August 2024 and April 2025 as it closed in on the largest fentanyl bust in U.S. history. The AP based its tally on thousands of pages of court documents, investigative records, detailed wiretap reports and 12 hours of DEA surveillance footage showing dealers moving large packages of pills in plastic bins and duffel bags that passed through highly transited hotels, apartment complexes, Airbnb rentals and self-storage facilities in six states. The Mexican president in her comments Thursday called the DEA's decision to permit fentanyl to hit the streets the "Fast and Furious of Fentanyl," a reference to the 2011 gun-walking scandal in which straw buyers smuggled some 2,000 assault weapons into Mexico with the intent of tracing the firearms to cartel leaders. "What is the United States doing in the United States?" Sheinbaum asked. "We have a prosecutor's office here, and the Security Ministry works here. So they should pay close attention to the other side of the border." The DEA did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Cole said a channel for submitting tips about the state of Jalisco would be made public Thursday. The state is a stronghold of the powerful Jalisco New Generation Cartel, known by its Spanish initials CJNG, which Washington also designated a terrorist organization. Meanwhile, a veteran DEA agent also told CBS News last month the agency has contributed to the problem by allowing fentanyl pills to reach the streets. "For three years, I've told my DEA managers that we're allowing dangerous amounts of fentanyl to hit the street, and we're doing nothing to stop it, and they didn't listen to me," DEA Special Agent David Howell told CBS News in his first television interview. articles.title: Andrea Stewart-Cousins, 1st Black woman to lead N.Y. Senate, dies at 76
articles.summary: ALBANY, New York — Democratic state Senate Majority Leader Andrea Stewart-Cousins, one of the highest-ranking Black women in New York state history, died Thursday evening, state officials announced Friday. “Throughout her decades in public service, Stewart-Cousins made a profound impact on the lives of New Yorkers,” New York Senate Democratic spokesperson Mike Murphy said. “She was a groundbreaking leader who shattered one of New York's highest glass ceilings, becoming the first woman to lead the New York State Senate.” Stewart-Cousins, 76, was reelected earlier this month to the top job in the Democratic-dominated chamber. She was preparing to preside over her party’s largest majority in modern history after Democrats captured at least 47 seats in the 63-member state Senate. It was too soon to determine Friday afternoon if Democrats will launch a race to succeed her or move forward with an interim leader. A Yonkers lawmaker, Stewart-Cousins was the first Black woman to lead what had been a notoriously fractious state Senate, which had long been ruled by Republicans. When Democrats came to power in 2019, Stewart-Cousins and state lawmakers passed a series of long-sought measures including criminal justice law changes and provisions like early voting. Known for wearing colorful scarfs, her friendly public demeanor obscured a hard-nosed tactician with a sarcastic streak. Behind the scenes she wouldn’t hesitate to discipline unruly rank-and-file members. Her death comes weeks before an Albany legislative session that’s expected to include debates over raising taxes and how to address voters’ sustained affordability concerns. “We’re going to be looking at the needs of New York, continuing to focus on affordability, the lives of working people, trying to figure out how to get the things people need,” Stewart-Cousins said in an interview with POLITICO earlier this month. Stewart-Cousins had been presiding over a Democratic conference in transition. Her longtime deputy, Mike Gianaris of Queens, retired in August, and she had batted away questions about her own retirement. Her ascension to Senate majority leader added the first woman to Albany’s fabled “three men in a room” — shorthand for the closed-door budget negotiations between the governor and legislative leaders. The role made Stewart-Cousins one of the most powerful elected officials in New York. She came out of the Westchester County Legislature. While serving there, she learned how to balance competing factions in a county whose demographics roughly mirror those of the state’s. It was there that she also developed her signature sartorial choice — always wearing a scarf, which she said she started doing because people confused her with the only other Black woman to win a seat at the county level. She first ran for Senate in 2004, losing by 18 votes. When she won two years later, she joined a tumultuous Democratic conference, with her first years in Albany marked by bitter feuds and power struggles. Her colleagues elevated her to minority leader in 2012 after her predecessor joined a long list of top senators facing indictments. Against all odds, she made it work. Democrats won 39 of the Senate’s 63 seats in 2018, giving members their first stable majority since World War II. And unlike every other modern instance when Senate Democrats won power, the conference under her leadership remained unified. It became the norm for socialists and moderates alike to begin their public statements with encomiums of “the tremendous leadership of our Andrea Stewart-Cousins.” “Most peoples’ experiences in the New York State Legislature involve a leader and a staff that would set the tone more than the members themselves,” Gianaris said in 2020 about her leadership style. “And Andrea takes a very different approach, where it’s the members that drive the decisions, and members that drive the agenda … It’s a much more bottom-up process than top-down.” The Senate long had a reputation as the place where progressive priorities met their demise in deep-blue New York. But it became arguably the center of left-leaning activism as soon as Stewart-Cousins became majority leader in 2019. The Legislature spent that year rapidly passing bottled-up legislation on subjects like immigration, tenant rights, and codifying abortion protections — a personal priority for her. Joe Anuta contributed to this report. This article originally appeared on Politico at https://www.politico.com/news/2026/11/27/trailblazing-ny-senate-majority-leader-dies-at-76-01184412
articles.author: Nick Reisman and Bill Mahoney

articles.title: Sen. Deb Fischer's husband died by suicide, her office says
articles.summary: Washington — Nebraska Sen. Deb Fischer's husband, Bruce Fischer, died by suicide, a spokesperson for her office said Friday. On Monday, the Republican senator's office announced that he had died Sunday, "peacefully while doing what he loved most, spending time outdoors." But on Friday, a spokeperson for Fischer's office said in a statement on X , "Initially, it was believed that Bruce passed peacefully at home. Upon further investigation, it was learned that Bruce chose to end his life. The family is deeply grateful for the recent outpouring of sympathy for their loss, and asks for understanding in this time of mourning." Fischer's office said no further details would be provided at this time. When the senator announced her husband's death earlier this week, she referred to him as "my partner in life, my greatest source of strength, and the heart of our family." They were married for 54 years. According to her Senate profile, Fischer met her husband, a cattle rancher, while she was a student at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln. After they married, the two moved to the family ranch outside of Valentine, Nebraska, where they raised their three sons. "His kindness, integrity, and quiet strength left a lasting impression on all who knew him," Fischer said of her late husband, adding that she "will cherish the decades we spend building a family in the Nebraska Sandhills." Fischer, 75, has represented Nebraska in the Senate since 2013. If you or someone you know may be experiencing a mental health crisis, contact the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline by dialing or texting "988." articles.title: U.S. strikes another merchant ship as its blockade of Iranian ports continues
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — The U.S. military has disabled a merchant ship in the Gulf of Oman that was trying to run its blockade of Iranian ports, U.S. Central Command said Friday. A military aircraft fired “precision munitions” at the stern of the Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer on Thursday, and the "ship’s propulsion was ultimately disabled and the civilian crew was unharmed,” it said in a statement. According to U.S. Central Command, the Pacific Archer left the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas before it attempted to run the blockade. Ship tracking websites list the vessel's destination as Singapore. The commander of the Iranian navy, Shahram Irani, said Friday on state television that Iran will carry out operations “that will not only break the naval blockade but also drive the enemy out of the region’s waters.” The strike comes as the Trump administration weighs its options in the long-simmering war with Iran, which began at the end of February and has settled into a quiet stalemate in the past several months. Earlier in November, officials in the region told The Associated Press that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was pushing the U.S. to restart the war or allow Israel to launch airstrikes on Iran’s nuclear facilities and missile capabilities. Meanwhile, government and security officials from the Persian Gulf countries, as well as Pakistan and Turkey, were engaged in a diplomatic campaign, which included phone calls with senior U.S. officials, to stave off a renewed war in the region. President Donald Trump has oscillated between threatening additional large-scale strikes on Iran and insisting that the war “militarily is effectively over.” The U.S. military has maintained a sizable naval force in the region, including a constant presence of two aircraft carriers and a host of other ships. The U.S. has been blockading Iranian ports since April, though the blockade was lifted in the summer during talks with Tehran and resumed in July. Since then, the U.S. military says it has redirected 158 merchant ships and disabling those that refuse to comply. The Pacific Archer is at least the 15th disclosed vessel to be disabled by the U.S. military since the blockade began in the spring and the sixth since it resumed this summer. The previous vessel was disabled on Nov. 7. In June, the practice drew condemnation when a military strike on a Guinea-Bissau-flagged tanker attempting to evade the American blockade resulted in three deaths. Three Indian sailors were killed when American forces struck the Palau-flagged M/T Settebello, officials in India said at the time. The leader of the International Maritime Organization, a United Nations agency, condemned the attack. U.S. Central Command has consistently said that American forces issue multiple warnings before firing on the merchant ships. Iran’s Revolutionary Guard said on Friday that two tankers attempted to transit the Strait of Hormuz through an “unauthorized” route, claiming that one of them struck a naval mine while the other was forced to turn back. The claims could not be independently verified. In a statement carried by Iran’s state broadcaster, the country’s Revolutionary Guard also said the number of oil tankers attempting to transit through unauthorized routes in the critical waterway has sharply decreased in recent days. Iran continues to warn ships not to pass through the strategic shipping lane without approval from Tehran. Oil flows in the first two weeks of November fell by around 20% to around 13 million barrels per day compared with October, when exports roughly equaled the prewar amounts of 15-16 million barrels per day, according to Rystad Energy. Reasons for the November decline include Iranian attacks that discourage tankers from attempting the strait crossing and reduced flows through a key Saudi pipeline to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, which has also been attacked several times. A report by U.N. Trade and Development finds that disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea, the Black Sea and the Panama Canal are lengthening voyages, raising fuel costs, driving port congestion and adding to uncertainty. Alternative ports, inland transport and logistics arrangements have kept trade moving, but at a higher cost. ___ Toqa Ezzidin in Cairo contributed. articles.title: Netflix drops schizophrenia scene from Tyson Fury doc after wife retracts claim
articles.summary: Tyson Fury does not have schizophrenia and a scene in which his wife claims he does has been edited out of the Netflix movie about the British boxing superstar. The doc, titled Tyson Fury, provides a tell-all account of Fury’s mental health struggles as he builds up to his fight with Anthony Joshua next month, which is also on Netflix. articles.title: Nvidia Blackwell chips turn up at China site tied to alleged spy Alice Huang
articles.summary: (Bloomberg) -- A pair of Chinese firms installed Nvidia Corp.’s powerful Blackwell semiconductors in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, the woman at the heart of a controversy surrounding the US chipmaker. Most Read from Bloomberg SAP Weighs Cutting at Least 10,000 Roles in AI Restructure Trump Calls GDP Numbers ‘Fake,’ Demands Probe After Revision South Africa Sentences Russia Army Recruit as Ukraine Urges Action Nvidia Rehires Huang in Stunning Reversal After Trump Push Billions in Data Center Deals Grind to Halt After Chip Curbs The gear installed at the Yangtze River Delta Project included a GB300 NVL72 rack, among Nvidia’s most powerful products, according to a serial number specified in documents submitted to Chinese regulators in November. Shanghai Shuoyao offered the hardware as collateral to obtain a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank, according to filings from the lender that were reviewed by Bloomberg News. A second firm Shanghai Kezhan, controlled by a Tokyo-based parent, described a GB200 server — which also relies on Blackwell chips — at the facility. That description was provided in documents when it obtained a 90 million yuan loan in late 2025 from a finance-leasing firm wholly owned by a local Shanghai government agency. The submissions reveal for the first time that Nvidia’s Blackwell processors found their way into a Chinese data center that has ties to Alice Huang and Megaspeed. These processors were until recently Nvidia’s most powerful data center products, and they’ve always been illegal to ship to China without a US license. President Donald Trump has explicitly said he doesn’t want these chips — which OpenAI and Anthropic PBC use to train their most cutting-edge models — going to the Asian country, at least for now. Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, meanwhile, once claimed they were too big to smuggle: a standard two-meter-tall GB300 NVL72 server rack, which contains 72 Blackwell Ultra chips and 36 Grace processors, can weigh more than 1,500 kilograms (3,300 pounds) and is about the size of a gigantic fridge. Nvidia and its just-reinstated CEO have come under intense scrutiny in recent weeks for their failure to stop diversion of the company’s products to China, a shadow trade that US officials believe is worth billions of dollars. It’s unclear how the GB300 rack made its way to the country, to Shanghai Shuoyao or to this specific site — described in local media as designed to house as many as 800,000 servers. By inputting the serial number for the product into a public warranty database, Bloomberg found that it was manufactured by Taiwan’s Gigabyte Technology Co., which assembles Nvidia chips into servers and racks. The database also provided a model name for the serial number, which matches a GB300 NVL72 server rack manufactured by the Taiwanese company. This sort of gear often passes through several hands — including local distribution networks — before it’s installed in data centers. In many cases, products that were ultimately smuggled into China were originally sold to parties in unrestricted areas. Bloomberg provided the rack’s serial number to Gigabyte, seeking information about to whom Gigabyte had originally sold the hardware and when. It declined to answer those questions, citing company policy. The firm “conducts all business in compliance with applicable laws and regulations,” a spokesperson said in an emailed statement. “All transactions are subject to our internal compliance requirements and the relevant laws and regulations in effect at the time.” Shanghai Shuoyao — the company that procured the GB300 rack and offered it as collateral — is active at the data center linked to Alice Huang and also has significant overlap with Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is under US investigation over concerns that it smuggled Nvidia chips to China, Bloomberg has reported. Shanghai Shuoyao, which hasn’t responded to Bloomberg queries over the past year, confirmed this month in a rare public statement that it is one of Megaspeed’s service providers, describing the partnership as “limited to ordinary commercial cooperation.” Megaspeed, meanwhile, used a rendering of the Yangtze River Delta Project in 2024 to describe its largest data center to investors, dubbing the site a “specific area” facility in an unnamed country. Bloomberg does not have evidence that Megaspeed itself diverted Nvidia hardware there, and Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing in response to the US probe. The company has not answered repeated queries about the Yangtze River Delta Project. Nor has Nvidia, which for years insisted that there was no black market for its products and didn’t respond to questions for this story. The Trump administration this month put Megaspeed on a US trade blacklist, citing a significant risk of involvement in chip diversion. Alice Huang in 2023 founded Megaspeed, a so-called neocloud that won a coveted stamp of approval from Nvidia within four days of its creation, and went on to become the chipmaker’s largest Southeast Asian customer. She also has ties to a number of companies that invested in the Yangtze River Delta Project, which counts Kang Wei as its president. Kang has been introduced at times as Alice Huang’s romantic partner, people familiar with the matter said. It’s unclear how far along operators are in meeting their overall goal for that project, which at 800,000 servers would be on par with hyperscale facilities used by companies like OpenAI. It’s also unclear what mix of servers they plan to use. The parameters they’ve outlined in construction plans reviewed by Bloomberg — specifically, the total processing power as compared to the energy input — would be extremely difficult to satisfy with chips from Chinese companies such as Huawei Technologies Co. Still, the smuggled hardware disclosed in the filings reviewed by Bloomberg is just a fraction of what they’d need. These documents only cover hardware offered as collateral for loans — providing a small snapshot of the operators’ ambitions, while also underscoring how some Chinese financial institutions, including with government ties, were aware that restricted hardware was getting into China and willing to lend capital on those assets. Bloomberg was unable to reach the leasing company that lent money to Shanghai Kezhan, nor Shanghai Innovation Bank, which in addition to the money it lent Shanghai Shuoyao, also provided a 200 million yuan loan to another company called Shanghai Longjie, similarly with restricted Nvidia chips as collateral. Shanghai Longjie — which has the same parent company as Shanghai Shuoyao — disclosed in documents filed to regulators that it has servers containing Nvidia’s earlier Hopper-generation chips, which are illegal to ship to China without Washington’s permission, Bloomberg reported this month. That hardware was manufactured by Super Micro Computer Inc. and Dell Technologies Inc. It’s unclear whether the shipments had US approval. Those aren’t the only Hopper chips at the Yangtze River Delta Project. Shanghai Kezhan, the company that described the GB200 server in filings last year, also disclosed that it has 32 servers with H200 chips there. These products had a Gigabyte prefix in their model name, but the documents didn’t include serial numbers — making them harder to trace. Shanghai Kezhan is headquartered about half a kilometer from the Yangtze River Delta Project, at the same commercial complex where Shanghai Shuoyao solicited engineers to work on Nvidia H100 and H200 chips — two restricted models. In February 2024, both of these firms added “imports and exports” to their business activities, according to data from Qizhidao, a company information provider. The same month, Megaspeed’s original parent — the Chinese gaming giant 7Road — obtained 16.7% of Shanghai Kezhan via a subsidiary the gaming company bought from Alice Huang in 2019. The other 83.3% of Kezhan is ultimately owned by NeXPower Japan, according to Qizhidao. Japan’s official companies registry returned only one company named NeXPower, which was established in March 2025. Caixin, a Chinese business news outlet, said the Tokyo firm is controlled by Alice Huang. Bloomberg has been unable to reach NeXPower for comment. Chinese-speaking staffers at the firm’s registered address wouldn’t confirm that was NeXPower’s office, and shut the door after Bloomberg News asked about their relationship with Alice Huang and Shanghai Kezhan. On the intercom was a message saying they are working and will not respond to media questions. The registered address of the company’s director appeared to be a vacated residence. In May 2025, records compiled by Big Trade Data show, Shanghai Kezhan received a shipment worth $11 million, flown from Malaysia to Shanghai Pudong International Airport with the company as consignee. The customs document described the shipment as “storage chassis,” referring to a structure that houses components of a storage server. But the product code it was assigned to was 847150, which denotes computing servers. The shipment’s unit price was $264,108, too costly for a storage chassis — but within the price range of servers powered by Nvidia’s Hopper chips. --With assistance from Mari Kiyohara, Natsuko Katsuki and Mayumi Negishi. articles.title: Lutnick in the hot seat as senators vow to crack down on AI chip leaks to China
articles.summary: Senators in both parties say that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is in the hot seat in the wake of revelations that Nvidia sold billions of dollars’ worth of high-tech chips to a Singapore-based company whose former senior executive, Alice Huang, is accused of being a Chinese spy. Lawmakers in both parties criticized President Trump’s intervention to persuade Nvidia’s board to bring Jensen Huang back as its CEO after he admitted to the extramarital affair with Alice Huang, whom American intelligence said had contact with a Chinese spy agency. But while senators have limited ability to change Nvidia’s decision to rehire Jensen Huang, they can exert more pressure on Lutnick, whose department depends on appropriations from Congress. Mark Warner (D-Va.), the incoming chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee who also sits on the Senate Banking Committee, which will hear testimony from Huang next week. Warner suggested the Commerce Department may have allowed Nvidia to make sensitive technology sales to companies in addition to Megaspeed, the company connected to Alice Huang, that undermined restrictions on China’s access to advanced chips. “The idea that the Commerce Department has been allowing potentially not just some of these one-off descriptions of [chip sales] that Nvidia’s been doing but through other Chinese shell companies — we deserve answers,” he said. Sen. Tom Cotton (R-Ark.), the current chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, said he had warned the Trump administration that advanced chips were getting past export controls and called on Congress to pass legislation to tighten restrictions. “Congress has much to investigate and we will pass overwhelmingly bipartisan chip export-control bills, including my Chip Security Act, one way or the other,” Cotton posted on the social platform X. Lutnick is coming under heavy scrutiny from both Democrats and Republicans on Capitol Hill after media outlets reported that he resisted pressure from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Secretary of State Marco Rubio to put Megaspeed, the company previously affiliated with Alice Huang, on a trade blacklist. Bessent confronted Lutnick earlier this month over why the Commerce Department had not banned the sale of advanced AI chips to Megaspeed, according to The New York Times. Bessent told CNBC in an interview that he was frustrated over the delay in restricting chip sales and blamed the Commerce Department for not acting. “I am frustrated when President Trump made it very clear China should not receive any Nvidia chips above H100s,” he said, adding that the Commerce Department “has the pen” and suggesting that it should explain “their internal processes.” Democrats, who will control the Senate and House in January, are pressing for answers about whether Lutnick may have been motivated by a financial conflict of interest. They want to know whether data centers in Southeast Asian countries that supplied advanced computing power to China had financial ties to Cantor Fitzgerald, the financial services firm that Lutnick once led and is now run by his sons. Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Md.), the incoming chair of the House Judiciary Committee, said Lutnick and other members of the Trump administration may “have converging personal, political, corporate and financial interests in making sure” Jensen Huang remains as Nvidia’s CEO. Lawmakers want to know what role Lutnick may have played in delaying the implementation of rules to restrict the sale of chips to companies such as Megaspeed and A201, a data center based in Malaysia, that allegedly provided China access to advanced computing power. The Commerce Department has said Lutnick has complied with all ethics rules. But key Republicans have joined Democrats in calling on Lutnick to testify about his role overseeing policies and regulations on chip exports. Senate Banking Committee Chair Tim Scott (R-S.C.) has asked Lutnick to appear before his panel next month to answer questions. Sen. John Kennedy (R-La.) said the Commerce Department appeared to “knowingly” allow sensitive AI technology to skirt export restrictions. “It appears that they knowingly allowed this to happen. Scott Bessent has been saying, ‘Stop it.’ So I want to get both of them in front of a committee, put them under oath,” he said on NBC’s “Meet the Press.” “If Secretary Lutnick is giving our chips away, he needs to stop it, in my opinion,” he added. This has prompted speculation on Capitol Hill that Lutnick’s future leadership of the Commerce Department could be on shaky ground. Lutnick will have to answer tough questions about a new report in The Atlantic that he transferred federal agents who were tasked with investigating the smuggling of advanced AI chips to his personal security detail, taking those agents off a critical national security job. Incoming Senate Commerce Committee Chair Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.) said she has “great concerns about his leadership of Commerce.” Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N.C.), a member of the Senate Banking Committee, said Lutnick should resign amid reports that the Commerce Department slow-walked export controls for AI chips. Tillis said Lutnick was briefed on the findings by U.S. intelligence agencies that Huang was having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy before Trump invited the Nvidia CEO to join him on Air Force One in Alaska en route to a trip to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing. He said Lutnick should have intervened to block Huang from joining the president, something that Rubio tried to do. “It was my understanding that Lutnick had been briefed on it too. Let’s just say for the sake of argument that the president was distracted and did not remember telling him about it. Lutnick should have damn well should have known,” Tillis said. He said it was not appropriate for Huang to join Trump on the high-level trip. He also cited what he called Lutnick’s “entanglements with investments in Nvidia.” Asked if Lutnick should resign, Tillis said: “I think he should roll.” The Hill reached out to the Commerce Department for comment. articles.title: 美国10月贸易逆差创一年半新高：受AI基建推动，进口额刷新历史纪录
articles.summary: AI基础设施建设热潮正把美国的贸易账目推向新的失衡高度。10月商品贸易逆差扩大10.7%至1495亿美元，进口跃升6.1%至3653亿美元，创1992年有统计以来的最高纪录，贸易可能在第四季度继续拖累经济增长。 美国商务部周五公布的数据显示， 进口增长呈现全面开花态势，资本品、汽车、工业用品和消费品悉数上扬，反映内需依旧强劲。 企业大举押注AI，但相关基础设施严重依赖进口，而进口在GDP核算中属于减项。 FWDBONDS首席经济学家Christopher Rupkey直言， 10月商品贸易逆差恶化将拖累第四季度经济增长，资本品进口激增表明AI并不总是带来更快的美国经济增长。 高盛经济学家也将第四季度GDP增速预估下调0.2个百分点至2.2%。 这一数据发布之际，特朗普政府本周提议对包括中国、日本和欧盟在内的14个主要贸易伙伴设定20%至40%的最高潜在关税税率。特朗普为关税辩护称其有必要缩小贸易逆差并重振美国工业基础，但进口在其任内仍以快速步伐增长。 逆差创3月以来最高，远超预期 美国商务部普查局数据显示，10月商品贸易逆差跳增10.7%，即144亿美元，至1495亿美元，为2025年3月以来最高水平。 路透调查的经济学家此前预估逆差为1330亿美元，实际数据明显恶化。 商品进口激增6.1%，即211亿美元，至3653亿美元，为1992年政府开始追踪该系列数据以来的最高水平。其中资本品领涨，增幅达8.5%，同比更是飙升80.0%。 进口的普遍上涨覆盖各大类别：消费品进口增长2.6%，其他商品进口增长4.5%，包含原油和非货币黄金的工业用品进口增长6.0%，汽车、发动机及零部件进口加速增长4.1%，食品、饲料和饮料进口上升2.5%。 国内需求保持旺盛是进口持续攀升的底层动力。包括企业投资和消费者支出在内的国内需求，在第三季度以五年多来最快的速度增长。 出口温和增长，难敌进口冲击。 商品出口10月增长3.2%，即67亿美元，至2158亿美元，但增幅远不及进口。 分项看，工业用品出口增长4.9%，资本品出口增长3.4%，汽车、发动机及零部件出口大涨5.7%，消费品出口增长4.2%。但食品、饲料和饮料出口大幅下滑7.9%，成为出口端的主要拖累。 AI对GDP的贡献被进口稀释 企业正在激进地为AI砸钱，让这项技术在经济中占据显眼位置。但AI基础设施的建设严重依赖进口，而进口是GDP增长的减项。这形成了一个微妙的经济账：企业支出数据看起来很亮眼，但对GDP的实际拉动却打了折扣。 高盛经济学家在报告中指出， 今年资本品进口的激增，正是AI对GDP的贡献低于企业支出数据所显示水平的原因之一。 FWDBONDS的Rupkey对此总结得更为直白：资本品进口激增，说明AI并不总是带来更大的美国经济增长。 政府周三公布的数据显示，贸易在第三季度从GDP增长中削减了3.21个百分点。不过，这一拖累被消费支出和企业设备投资（主要是AI相关）的强劲增长所抵消。第三季度经济按年率计算增长4.3%，高于4至6月期间的2.2%。贸易已连续四个季度未能对GDP增长作出贡献。 库存回补或缓冲四季度冲击 贸易逆差对本季度GDP增长的冲击，可能因企业为满足需求而重建库存而得到缓解。 美国普查局周五同日公布的数据显示， 10月批发库存增长0.9%，高于9月的0.8%，其中耐用品库存跳升1.6%是主要推手。零售库存增长0.8%，前值为0.7%。汽车及零部件经销商库存大增1.3%，高于9月的0.6%增幅。 剔除汽车及零部件后，零售库存10月增长0.6%，9月为增长0.7%。这一分项将计入GDP核算。 库存投资在连续五个季度下降后于第三季度反弹，上季度为GDP增长贡献了1.64个百分点。 高盛经济学家将第四季度GDP增长预估下调0.2个百分点至2.2%的年率。该预估已计入10月批发和库存数据，他们认为这些数据部分抵消了巨额贸易逆差带来的拖累。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 金属大反攻！伦铜创九个月最大日涨，纽银涨近8%，AI恐慌缓解、中国稳市信号提振
articles.summary: 经历此前一轮集中抛售后，金属市场周五迎来强势反攻，铜、黄金和白银集体走高。伦铜创九个月来最大单日涨幅，COMEX白银期货涨近8%。AI交易恐慌缓解、中国释放稳市信号，推动市场风险偏好回暖；但这轮上涨究竟意味着趋势反转，还是超跌后的仓位修复，仍有待观察。 市场情绪从低谷回暖，伦铜一度涨超6% 周五，LME三个月期铜收涨约3.2%，报12251美元/吨，盘中一度上涨6.4%，创2月以来最大单日涨幅。全周累计上涨约0.75%，结束三周连跌。 上海期货交易所主力铜合约收涨5.5%，盘中涨幅一度达7.1%；COMEX 12月期铜收涨3.38%，创4月8日以来最大日涨幅，报5.517美元/磅，全周上涨约0.58%，终结六周连跌。 此前，铜价经历了11月以来的剧烈调整。周三，LME期铜一度跌至每吨11650美元，为11个月低位；COMEX铜期货也跌至去年12月以来低点。市场担忧AI投资热潮能否持续，叠加美元走强、利率上行和交易所库存增加，令铜价承压。 周五的反攻则与市场风险偏好回暖同步。AI相关股票止跌回升，缓解了此前围绕数据中心投资和科技股估值的担忧；中国释放稳股市信号，也为市场情绪提供支撑。 盛宝银行（Saxo Bank）大宗商品策略主管Ole Hansen指出： “虽然这与工业金属没有直接关系，但在市场情绪相当低迷之际，这是市场迫切需要的积极信号。” 不过，铜价短线反弹并不意味着供需压力已经消失。全球主要交易所监测的铜库存本周继续增加，累计升至约110.5万吨，为五个月高位；过去八周中，库存有七周增加。与此同时，AI数据中心建设对铜需求的长期支撑仍在，但市场正在重新评估相关投资的增长速度和持续性。 中国现货市场的需求信号也值得关注。周五洋山铜溢价约为每吨320美元，虽然低于此前一度达到的500美元纪录高位，但仍处于较高水平。此前为应对美国关税预期而提前运往美国的部分铜库存，正受到中国较高溢价吸引，可能转向中国市场。 黄金白银结束连跌，白银涨幅接近8% 贵金属同样大幅走高。COMEX 12月黄金期货周五收涨2.94%，报3639.60美元/盎司，全周累涨3.53%。盘中期金曾涨破3680美元、日内涨超4%。 白银表现更为强劲。COMEX 12月白银期货周五收涨7.76%，创2月3日以来最大单日涨幅，报43.167美元/盎司，全周累涨5.11%，和期金均结束两周连跌。 需要注意的是，11月26日美国感恩节期间，纽约黄金、白银和铜期货市场没有常规交易。因此，周五上述期货合约的日涨幅，是相对于11月25日周三收盘价计算的，包含了周四休市期间的价格间隔，不能简单与正常交易周五的单日涨幅直接比较。 此前，黄金和白银也遭遇了明显抛售。随着AI相关资产大幅波动，投资者为满足流动性需求而出售部分持仓，贵金属未能充分发挥避险属性，反而受到资产抛售和美元走强的双重压力。感恩节假期期间，科技股抛售和资产清算暂歇，也为贵金属提供了喘息空间。 白银涨幅明显超过黄金，一方面反映其在市场风险偏好改善时通常具有更高的价格弹性，另一方面也与其工业金属属性有关。电子产品和AI产业链需求预期，仍是影响白银市场情绪的因素之一。 美联储政策预期仍是贵金属反弹的关键制约 尽管金银周五大幅上涨，但宏观环境尚未出现根本性变化。市场仍在评估美联储12月加息以及明年进一步收紧政策的可能性。美元和实际利率维持高位，意味着持有黄金等无息资产的机会成本仍然偏高。 Audacity Capital分析师Zain Vawda认为，近期金价回升更像是空头回补和获利了结，而不是市场趋势发生改变。他表示： “近期这轮反弹看起来更像是空头回补和获利了结，而不是趋势发生了改变。美联储还将加息，实际收益率处于高位，美元也接近数月高点。” Vawda还指出，在上述因素发生变化之前，金价反弹至3750至3800美元/盎司附近可能重新遭遇卖盘。 对于铜而言，短期交易情绪能否持续改善，以及库存增长是否放缓，将是判断反弹持续性的关键；长期来看，电气化、发电设施和电网建设仍构成需求支撑。贵金属则更直接受到美元、实际利率和资金流向影响。 因此，周五的金属市场大反攻，更多反映了此前集中抛售后的风险偏好修复和仓位调整。随着下周市场恢复正常交易，AI投资预期、库存变化和美联储政策信号能否继续支持价格，将成为检验这轮反弹成色的关键。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: OpenAI反击苹果！指控其窃取商业机密、威胁供应商，双方诉讼战升级
articles.summary: OpenAI向苹果发起反诉，指控这家科技巨头窃取其商业机密、阻断其硬件供应商渠道，两家曾经的合作伙伴之间的法律对抗正迅速激化。 周五，OpenAI在加州法院提起诉讼，回击苹果于今年夏天对其提出的商业秘密窃取指控。OpenAI在诉状中措辞强硬，指控苹果"以一切可用手段实施不公平竞争"，涵盖"多种违法、不公平及侵权行为"。 此次法律摩擦对两家公司的关系造成进一步损害。就在两年前，双方还达成合作协议，将ChatGPT嵌入iPhone。 如今随着OpenAI加速布局硬件领域，直接与苹果形成竞争态势，双方关系已急剧恶化。这场法律战的走向，将对两家公司在AI硬件及供应链领域的竞争格局产生深远影响。 苹果股价周五收涨0.83%。 OpenAI反诉：苹果"威胁"共同供应商 OpenAI在诉状中指控苹果利用其"体量与财富阻碍竞争"，具体手段包括向同时为OpenAI提供服务的供应商施压，实施"胁迫和威胁"。 这一指控的背景是：OpenAI去年5月斥资64亿美元收购了由苹果前首席设计官Sir Jony Ive领衔的设计工作室io，并正筹备推出一系列新型个人智能设备。 OpenAI称，这些产品有望"在苹果视为自身腹地的领域超越苹果"。 苹果长期以来凭借供应链掌控能力巩固竞争优势——通过预付资金锁定关键零部件和制造产能，确保旗下产品率先获得最新芯片。但OpenAI指控苹果此次的行为已越界，借助供应链影响力直接压制竞争对手。 员工流动成为双方争议核心 这场法律战的另一条主线，是双方围绕离职员工的互相指控。 苹果于今年7月起诉，指控数名前员工——包括现任OpenAI首席硬件官Tang Tan——向新东家泄露了涉及苹果产品研发及供应链的机密信息。苹果还指控另一名前工程师在离职后利用公司网络存储系统的"漏洞"窃取机密文件。 OpenAI于8月否认窃取苹果商业机密，并将苹果的诉讼定性为阻止其招募人才的手段。 在周五的反诉中，OpenAI将矛头转向苹果的内部管理做法，指控苹果鼓励员工将公司文件存储在个人设备和个人云存储账户中，从而为日后的法律追责埋下伏笔。 诉状援引了一句颇具挑衅意味的表述："苹果为员工设下了一个精妙的陷阱。那些聪明的年轻人以为自己要去库比蒂诺工作，却发现自己加入的是'加州旅馆'——你随时可以退房，但永远无法离开。" OpenAI同时指控，一名此前曾在OpenAI任职、后返回苹果的前员工，向苹果透露了OpenAI的产品计划及供应商信息。 曾经的合作伙伴，如今的正面竞争者 此次诉讼标志着两家公司关系的根本性转变。 两年前，苹果与OpenAI的合作协议曾被视为AI与消费电子融合的重要里程碑。而随着OpenAI通过收购io直接进军硬件领域，双方已从合作伙伴演变为正面竞争对手。 OpenAI即将推出的个人智能设备，将直接切入苹果赖以立足的核心市场。 在此背景下，供应链资源的争夺、人才的流动，以及商业机密的归属，均已成为双方博弈的关键战场。这场法律战的最终走向，或将在相当程度上影响AI硬件新赛道的竞争秩序。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 标普19个月最佳一周！美股AI交易巨震背后：黄仁勋回归、特朗普押注与监管风险交织
articles.summary: 黄仁勋重新执掌英伟达，点燃美股周初反弹，但AI交易随即再度遭遇剧烈震荡，Anthropic上市后首次破发、英伟达两日回吐近10%。特朗普政府的AI政策押注、科技巨头巨额资本开支引发的回报疑虑，以及监管和宏观政策风险，共同塑造了在巨震后仍大幅收涨的感恩节交易周。 黄仁勋回归引爆周一大反弹，AI交易两日抛售后周五回暖 11月23日周一，英伟达董事会宣布黄仁勋重新出任公司CEO，成为扭转此前美股科技股抛售行情的关键催化剂。此前，特朗普曾公开推动黄仁勋回归，白宫方面也参与了相关沟通。特朗普周一当天表示，黄仁勋重新执掌英伟达对公司乃至美国经济都很重要。 消息公布后，英伟达股价周一暴涨31.5%，单日市值增加近1万亿美元。纳指收涨6.51%，标普500指数涨4.73%，道指涨3.01%。AI产业链普遍反弹，AMD、美光、闪迪，以及CoreWeave、Nebius、IREN等数据中心和算力服务企业均大幅收涨。 但这场反弹很快遭遇考验。周二和周三，英伟达连续两个交易日下跌，累计跌幅约9.5%，AMD、美光等芯片股也重新承压。Anthropic则在上市第四个交易日、即11月24日周二，收盘跌至83美元IPO发行价下方，成为这轮AI交易降温的又一个标志性事件。 英伟达在黄仁勋辞职后上周累跌近23%，本周一大反弹超30%，周二和周三累跌约9.5%，周五小幅收涨 周三美股盘中一度出现新一轮抛售，纳指和标普500指数跌幅一度明显扩大，但尾盘买盘帮助市场收复大部分失地。周四感恩节休市后，周五市场重新转向上涨，科技股尤其是芯片和AI基础设施板块领涨。 三大指数周五集体收涨并创逾一周收盘新高，其中道指实现四连涨，创10月6日以来最长连涨日；此前连续两日下跌的标普500指数和纳指则双双反弹。 标普500指数周五收涨1.6%，本周累涨5.6%；道指收涨1.18%，全周累涨5.46%；纳指收涨2.31%，全周累涨6.68%，分别创2025年4月以来、2022年10月以来和今年4月17日以来最大单周涨幅。 三大美股指本周一集体大涨后表现分化，标普和纳指此后两连跌、周五反弹，道指全周四个交易日持续收涨 AI产业链的反弹也重新扩散。闪迪周五大涨约16%，美光上涨约7%，AMD以及光通信股Lumentum、Coherent等走强，CoreWeave、Nebius和IREN等数据中心企业也重新获得资金关注。 英伟达周五仅小幅收涨约0.8%，但由于周一涨幅巨大，全周仍累计上涨近19.9%。Anthropic则在周五大涨约11%，收于91.90美元附近，终于重新站上83美元IPO发行价，结束上市首周的破发阴影。媒体认为，Anthropic股价周五反弹，既受益于AI股票整体回暖，也反映出市场对这家创纪录IPO公司的风险偏好有所恢复。 值得注意的是，尽管本周三大指数录得显著涨幅，但仍未完全收复上周跌幅。上周标普500指数累计下跌8.61%，创2025年4月4日以来最大单周跌幅；道指和纳指分别下跌8.02%和10.02%，均创2020年3月以来最大单周跌幅。 因此，本周更准确的定性是一次大幅超跌后的修复，而不是美股已经重新确立了持续上涨趋势。 超跌回补与仓位反转推动反弹，AI产业链仍未走出调整 从全周表现看，这轮反弹的广度和幅度都相当突出，但不同股票之间的表现仍然存在明显差异。 费城半导体指数（SOX）全周累涨约9.3%，明显跑赢三大股指。此前遭遇重挫的芯片股重新成为资金回补的重点，闪迪、美光和AMD等受益于AI基础设施建设的公司表现尤其突出。光通信企业Coherent、Lumentum，以及CoreWeave、Nebius和IREN等AI算力基础设施企业，也随着风险偏好回升而反弹。 不过，英伟达和Anthropic的剧烈波动说明，投资者并没有因为本周反弹就彻底消除对AI交易的疑虑。 英伟达周一暴涨31.5%，随后两个交易日累计下跌约9.5%，周五仅小幅反弹；Anthropic上市第四个交易日便跌破发行价，直到周五才重新收复失地。两家公司一个代表AI算力产业链的核心，一个代表AI模型商业化的高估值标杆，其股价走势都反映出市场正在重新评估AI行业的投资回报与估值。 事实上，本周反弹的一个重要驱动力，可能并不是AI产业基本面发生了根本性改善，而是前一周极端抛售之后，投资者仓位和市场情绪出现了反转。 Harris Financial Group管理合伙人Jamie Cox的评论称： “市场已经严重超卖，反弹几乎不可避免。” 摩根士丹利投资管理公司高级投资组合经理Andrew Slimmon则从资金仓位角度解释了反弹为何可能延续： “此前有大量快钱已经从科技股中去杠杆，因此这轮反弹可能延续至下周，因为这些资金将被迫重新追入市场。” Slimmon还指出，科技股反弹从周一开始，周三盘中反转后延续至周五。此前快速撤离科技股的资金，可能需要重新买入以恢复仓位。 这也解释了为何本周AI股票能够在基本面疑虑尚未消除的情况下迅速反弹：此前集中减仓导致市场仓位偏低，而周一英伟达的意外反转又为投资者提供了重新入场的理由。超跌回补、空头回补和被动恢复仓位，共同放大了反弹幅度。 与此同时，美国经济数据表现出韧性，也为风险资产提供了一定支撑。本周公布的三季度经济增长数据强于预期，说明美国经济活动仍有一定动能。但通胀压力并未同步缓解，10月通胀加速，市场对美联储12月加息的预期几乎完全计价。 这意味着，经济韧性一方面支撑企业盈利预期，另一方面也可能让利率在更长时间内维持高位，对估值较高、融资需求较大的AI企业形成压力。 治理争议、贸易摩擦与监管审查，AI繁荣面临多重考验 如果说黄仁勋回归是本周美股反弹最直接的催化剂，那么特朗普政府对AI产业的政策押注，以及随之而来的政治和监管不确定性，则构成了这轮行情更深层的背景。 特朗普此前推动黄仁勋重新执掌英伟达，反映出美国政府对维持本国AI产业竞争优势的重视。英伟达不仅是美国科技行业的代表性企业，也是美国AI基础设施建设和全球算力竞争的重要支柱。 从这个角度看，黄仁勋回归不仅是一次企业管理层调整，也具有明显的政策和产业意义。市场最初将其解读为AI生态稳定性得到恢复，进而推动英伟达及其上下游企业集体反弹。 但特朗普政府对AI产业的支持，并不意味着行业面临的政策风险已经消失。 一方面，特朗普政府希望加快AI基础设施建设，保持美国在全球人工智能竞争中的领先地位；另一方面，贸易政策、芯片供应链限制以及数据中心建设面临的能源和土地使用问题，都可能影响AI产业的扩张节奏。 彭博社11月27日以特朗普的AI战略为切入点复盘本周行情，指出特朗普的政策押注与华尔街对AI交易的重新评估交织在一起，使这个感恩节交易周成为近年来波动最剧烈的交易周之一。 尤其值得关注的是美国国内政治环境的变化。民主党在中期选举中取得进展后，市场开始担忧AI行业可能面临更严格的监管审查。数据中心的电力消耗、基础设施建设对社区的影响，以及科技巨头在AI领域的市场支配力，都可能成为未来政策争论的焦点。 对于AI基础设施企业而言，这些风险并非抽象的政治议题。数据中心建设需要巨额资本投入，还涉及电力供应、土地审批、融资和长期客户合同。一旦监管趋严或项目审批放缓，即使AI需求继续增长，企业也可能面临投资回收周期拉长的问题。 黄仁勋回归本身也存在另一面。虽然特朗普推动其复职缓解了市场对英伟达领导层变动的担忧，但企业治理问题并未因此消失。 在被周五公布的采访中，Panmure Liberum策略主管Joachim Klement对黄仁勋回归提出了相当尖锐的批评： “这是一场公司治理噩梦。” Klement表示，他与多位大型ESG投资者交流后发现，这些投资者因公司治理方面的担忧，正在考虑出售英伟达股票。他认为，这可能在未来几周给英伟达股价带来额外抛售压力。 这说明，特朗普的支持虽然能够改变市场对英伟达短期经营稳定性的判断，却不能完全消除投资者对企业治理、监管审查和政治干预的担忧。 此外，特朗普政府本周提出新的关税措施，也令市场重新评估贸易摩擦和通胀风险。美股投资者需要同时应对AI产业政策、贸易政策和货币政策的不确定性，高估值科技股因此更容易出现剧烈波动。 全球市场风险偏好回暖，AI投资回报仍是核心考题 本周五，全球市场也出现了值得关注的积极信号。 中国方面，周五召开的国务院常务会议部署进一步稳定资本市场工作，强调增强资本市场内在稳定性、完善稳市机制，并提出发挥中央汇金等机构作用。新华社报道后，中国股市周五大幅上涨，沪深主要指数集体走强，半导体、AI和科技板块表现尤为突出。 主流媒体将中国政府释放的稳市信号视为推动亚洲市场反弹的重要因素，并指出沪深300周五录得两年来最大单日涨幅。韩国等亚洲市场也出现科技股反弹。 报道称韩国监管方考虑扩大股市稳定基金规模后，韩国股指周五收涨超4% 不过，对本周美股而言，全球市场情绪改善更多是辅助因素，真正决定行情走向的仍然是美国AI产业链的投资回报问题。 路透社在周五的市场复盘中指出，投资者本周在逢低买入与担忧AI支出、融资规模和投资回报之间反复摇摆。尽管周五科技股反弹，但标普500指数和纳指仍可能录得2008年以来最差的11月表现。 对于华尔街而言，接下来需要观察的并不是AI企业是否还会宣布新的资本开支计划，而是这些投入能否转化为持续的收入增长和现金流。 英伟达的芯片需求、AMD和存储芯片企业的订单增长，以及CoreWeave、Nebius和IREN等算力服务商的融资能力和盈利前景，都将成为市场判断AI产业链景气度的重要依据。 Anthropic的上市首周表现也提供了另一个观察窗口：即便拥有领先模型、快速增长的企业客户和创纪录的IPO规模，AI公司仍然需要面对高昂的算力成本、巨额基础设施承诺以及市场对估值的严格检验。 因此，本周美股创下逾一年多来的最佳单周表现，并不意味着AI交易的风险已经解除。黄仁勋回归暂时缓解了英伟达的领导层不确定性，超跌回补推动资金重新涌入科技股，特朗普政府的AI政策押注也为行业提供了部分政策预期支撑。 但高资本开支能否兑现为利润、融资成本是否继续上升，以及AI行业未来是否面临更严格的监管，仍将决定这轮反弹究竟是新一轮上涨的起点，还是剧烈调整中的阶段性修复。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 从铝市场逼空到LME紧急干预：一场库存危机如何将交易所推向险境？
articles.summary: 一场历史性的供应逼空正再度将伦敦金属交易所（LME）推向信任危机。 现货价格远高于期货、可用库存降至1990年以来最低，持有空头头寸的铝产业链企业承受数十年来最陡的展期成本。在实物用户密集施压后，LME本周紧急修改规则，试图遏制大型交易商对市场的挤压。 据彭博援引知情人士透露， LME本周二宣布缩短新冶炼厂注册交割的等待期，并批准印尼PT Hua Chin Aluminum Indonesia的金属自下周起交割；当日午后另一份通知进一步收紧大额持仓规则。 消息落地后一分钟内，市场最关注的现货对三个月期货价差从每吨400美元骤降至67美元。 不过，干预效果尚待观察。 价差在周四和周五重新走阔，尽管倒挂程度仍低于LME出手前。 摩根士丹利分析师Amy Gower在报告中指出，在库存重建之前，近端实物紧张可能持续。 从一致看空到剧烈逼空 上个月全球金属行业齐聚伦敦参加LME周时，市场对铝的共识是看空。 交易商和分析师预计，印尼中资新建冶炼厂将带来产量激增，推动市场转向过剩。 仅数周之后，11月初市场便陷入剧烈逼空。铝价随科技股及其他大宗商品一同下挫，但市场内部正在发生极端变化：现货价格远高于期货，交易所库存不断下降，即将到期的空头持仓者面临数十年来最高的溢价。 LME最初认为这反映了铝市的真实状况。供应紧张的理据确实充分：印尼供应激增尚未到来，中东大型冶炼厂生产受到伊朗战争冲击，交易所库存处于1990年以来最低水平。短期供应稀缺时，现货价格往往高于远期期货，形成倒挂结构。 但当11月主力合约上周到期却未出现实质性交割后，LME的立场开始转变。若市场必须等待印尼库存到货，极端倒挂可能持续数月。 对冲盘被迫平仓，产业链承压 据知情人士称，LME收到越来越多实物用户的求助电话。铝产业链企业普遍通过卖出期货对冲所持库存，市场转为倒挂后，展期将带来巨额亏损。本周倒挂最严重时，将现货合约展期至12月的成本为每吨250美元，相当于每月约8%。 许多企业无法通过向交易所交割来平仓，因为其产品并非可交割品。铝轧制厂可能用LME对冲风险，但其用于饮料罐和汽车车身的铝板并不符合LME合约交割标准；氧化铝交易商同样如此。 据交易商和高管称，行业企业开始抛售库存以逃离LME逼空。欧洲实物溢价（在LME价格之上支付的实物金属溢价）下跌超过一半。 CRU Group首席铝分析师Ross Strachan表示：“我确实不记得以前有过类似情况。现实是，这将从各个方面挤压价值链上不同环节的企业，而且冲击会很重。” Norsk Hydro ASA首席执行官Eivind Kallevik在采访中表示：“作为交易商，你可能只想看到这些情况如何演变、最终结局是什么，但对我们生产商和客户而言，LME保持相关性和良好运转至关重要。” 多重障碍阻断自我修复 理论上，逼空应当自我修正：倒挂加深会提高持货商向交易所交割的意愿，推动库存回升，终结短缺。 但铝市有几重因素使这一机制复杂化： 首先，LME合约所依托的铝几乎全部为俄罗斯原产，产自西方制裁禁止新俄铝交割之前。买家对其接受度低于其他产地金属，使其价值偏低，即便倒挂陡峭，交易商也不愿向LME交割非俄铝。 其次，中东生产商的大量库存因霍尔木兹海峡运输困难而滞留，难以进入LME全球仓储网络。 最后，印尼新冶炼厂产出的铝尚未完成交割注册。 新规落地，脆弱性犹存 据知情人士称，正是实物用户的这些呼声促使LME本周出手。自1996年一名违规铜交易员将LME推向崩溃边缘以来，该交易所不断推出规则以增强市场抗逼空能力。如今，2022年镍空头逼仓的记忆仍挥之不去。 周二上午，LME宣布缩短新冶炼厂注册交割前的等待期，加快印尼金属到货，并批准印尼PT Hua Chin Aluminum Indonesia自下周起交割。 当日下午约3时14分，另一份通知送达交易商邮箱，收紧大额持仓者的角色，即便其持仓低于可用库存的50%。价差随即崩塌，一名交易商调侃称，盈亏取决于读通知的速度。 但问题未必解决。 目前，LME在单一交易商持仓超过库存30%时，实际上为单日“Tom-next”倒挂设定了上限；若多名交易商各自买入略低于30%的库存，市场仍易受逼空冲击。 据知情人士称，颇具讽刺意味的是，部分交易商在LME干预前正准备交割金属，价差在干预后崩塌，他们随即改变计划。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 美国“黑五”购物季遇冷：消费者削减预算、缩短购物清单，折扣也难刺激消费
articles.summary: 美国最重要的购物季以低迷姿态拉开帷幕。消费者普遍压缩支出、精简礼品清单，部分门店员工数量甚至超过顾客。尽管折扣力度依然可观，但价格基数上移与消费心态趋谨，使得今年黑色星期五的气氛明显不及往年。 据彭博，购物中心客流稀疏，零售商感受到明显压力。 纽约曼哈顿一家豪华购物中心内，安保人员数量多于顾客；纽约郊区多处购物中心停车位充裕；一名在芝加哥沃尔玛购物的消费者表示，她今年的节日预算从2000美元直接腰斩至1000美元。 全美零售联合会（NRF）数据显示， 自疫情结束以来，今年假日购物周末的到场消费者人数预计将首次出现下滑，提前开启的分散促销活动令消费者在感恩节前便已分流。 尽管如此， 价格上涨与更早开始的促销活动仍可能推高整体消费总额。 普华永道预测，今年节日季总消费额将同比增长5.4%，扣除通胀后实际增幅为2.8%。Adobe Analytics数据显示，仅黑色星期五当日，美国消费者的线上交易额预计将接近130亿美元。 消费者勒紧腰带，购物策略趋于保守 走进今年黑色星期五的美国消费者，普遍带着更明确的节制意识。 在维吉尼亚州斯普林菲尔德好市多购物的Laura Forbes（46岁）直言，消费心态已悄然转变： "以前是'你想要什么？'现在变成了'你需要什么？'" 在新泽西州Millburn的Mall at Short Hills，22岁的Rose Lora表示： "我们还是会给人买礼物，但肯定会更谨慎一些。" 在缅因州Kittery Premium Outlets，28岁的Kayla Pinto驱车45分钟专程前来，她说消费者寻求的是"折上折"。在芝加哥沃尔玛购物的Carla Baeza则在采购一包5美元的15双装袜子，她表示："到处都在涨价，我们真的没有多少钱可花。" 51岁的Tarsha Rice今年凌晨12点半便已在维吉尼亚州Falls Church的Target门口排队，但她明确表示今年不打算购买新电子产品——"通常我们会升级换代，今年只是添置配件。"她估计自己的支出削减了30%至40%。"看看这些价格，消费能力已经大不如前了。" 消费结构生变，二手与体验式消费升温 今年的购物偏好出现结构性转变，消费者正在将注意力从电子产品等大件商品转向更具体验性的礼品类别。 普华永道调查显示，消费者越来越倾向于赠送"让人远离屏幕"的礼物，包括拼图、编织用品，以及音乐会、旅行和水疗日等体验类礼品。 二手购物需求同样升温——40%的消费者表示正在寻找二手或复古商品的折扣，较去年上升5个百分点。 囤货行为也在一定程度上扰乱了节日季的消费节奏。 受技术故障波及航班系统、通信服务器和银行系统等事件影响，部分消费者进入"备灾模式" ，沃尔玛、好市多和Tractor Supply等大型零售商此前迎来一波抢购潮，消费者争相囤积瓶装水、发电机乃至露营设备。 Adobe Analytics数据显示，11月前几周，家庭日用品支出激增，清洁产品、个人卫生用品及婴儿用品的消费额均较上月增长逾30%，导致部分商品在主力促销启动前便已售罄。 在马里兰州Potomac居住的Dale Yuzuki（63岁）原本计划趁黑色星期五购买发电机，并特意设置了比价提醒，但由于抢购潮提前爆发，他看中的型号已断货。"对我来说并不紧急，"他表示，即便折扣活动结束后商品才恢复库存，他仍会出手购买。 促销提前分流，到店人流下降 消费者的购物节奏正在改变，黑色星期五作为单一购物高峰的地位正被逐步稀释。 Circana全球思想领导力负责人Kiara Barrett指出，今年有更多消费者提前制定购物计划，"他们在拟定清单、锁定商品上更加有的放矢，然后等待折扣到位后再下单结账"。 这一趋势在实际购买行为上得到印证。33岁的Kelsi Jackson在11月初Lowe's的黑色星期五预售活动启动时便入手了一台新冰箱，折扣幅度约为36%。她此前已浏览比较过多次价格，最终决定"等到促销真正开始再买"。 沃尔玛方面也呈现出类似的前置消费信号。该公司11月19日披露，与去年同期相比，今年已多售出100万只火鸡。 其首席财务官John David Rainey表示，这一趋势可能预示消费者将在整个节日季提前展开购物。GlobalData常务董事Neil Saunders则指出，黑色星期五历来依赖大量冲动消费，"即便折扣仍在，很多商品的原始标价已经更高了"。 高收入群体撑起消费增量，整体动能趋弱 从宏观层面看，美国消费者进入节日季前的动能已出现边际放缓。 经通胀调整后，10月消费支出几乎没有增长，此前三季度的强劲势头明显降温，显示家庭在节日购物季正式启动前已出现消费停顿。 尽管今年大部分时间内，丰厚的税务退款、股市上涨以及相对低位的失业率对消费形成支撑，但食品与能源成本的再度抬升正在侵蚀家庭可支配预算。 NRF指出，节日消费增量大概率将由高收入群体主导，而更多普通消费者则计划削减礼品开支并积极寻找特价商品。 美国世界大型企业研究会的调查也印证了这一分化——仅年收入在20万美元及以上的群体表示，今年的节日消费将高于去年。 这一结构性分化，或将为本次节日购物季的整体成色蒙上阴影。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 日本烟草大涨！市场押注其与奥驰亚联手收购并分拆帝国品牌
articles.summary: 日本烟草股价近日表现亮眼。 市场押注该公司将与奥驰亚（Altria）联手，收购并拆分英国卷烟制造商帝国品牌（Imperial Brands）。 据 华尔街见闻此前文章 ，奥驰亚此前一天表示，正在考虑以全现金方式竞购帝国品牌，并已就收购其中部分业务与另一方展开讨论。据彭博报道，日本烟草正在评估与合作伙伴共同收购的方案。 帝国品牌表示尚未收到任何收购接洽，但会考虑任何提案。Jefferies 的 Andon-Ionita 认为，鉴于其关键美国业务和德国业务面临挑战，帝国品牌股东可能愿意接受市盈率高于过去五年 12 个月峰值 9.6 倍的报价。 这笔交易可能拉开烟草行业一轮大规模整合的序幕。随着许多市场的吸烟率长期下降，烟草公司正面临增长压力。奥驰亚、日本烟草和帝国品牌在培育新产品线方面均不及部分规模更大的竞争对手。 LSEG 数据显示，若交易完成，将是自 2016 年 British American Tobacco 以 600 亿美元（含债务）收购美国同业 Reynolds American 以来，该行业最大的一笔收购。 日本烟草ADR周五上涨2.4%，过去5天上涨10%。 日本烟草和奥驰亚收购帝国品牌合乎逻辑 帝国品牌旗下拥有 Davidoff、Gauloises 和 Kool 等卷烟品牌。分析师普遍认为，收购帝国品牌对日本烟草和奥驰亚都具有逻辑上的合理性，而合理的拆分路径是日本烟草接手其美国资产及部分区域业务，奥驰亚则取得其国际资产的全部或一部分。 日本烟草拥有 Camel、Benson & Hedges 等品牌，以及 Ploom 加热烟草设备系列，近年来一直在美国扩张，尤其是通过低价卷烟品牌抢占市场份额。 分析师认为，接手帝国品牌的美国资产将显著提升其在这一具有吸引力市场中的存在感。 Jefferies 分析师 Andrei Andon-Ionita 在给客户的报告中称， 这笔交易可能“将日本烟草转变为一家规模可观、多元化且估值合理的美国市场第三大竞争者，并具备成本协同潜力”。 对奥驰亚而言，接手帝国品牌的非美国业务将标志着其重返国际烟草销售。 二十年前，该公司剥离全球业务以专注美国市场。近年来，其在美国市场面临多重挑战。分析师表示，奥驰亚可借此进入烟草销量下滑幅度较小、且替代吸烟产品增长所受约束较少的地区，但协同效应有限。 财务影响看法分歧 分析师对收购方的财务影响看法不一。BTIG 分析师 Owen Bennett 在报告中称，这笔交易“可以在不影响双方当前信用评级的情况下完成”。 但晨星分析师 Kristoffer Inton 警告，这可能会将奥驰亚的净杠杆推至历史最高水平，即使暂停股票回购，也需要数年时间才能恢复目标杠杆。 截至 9 月底，日本烟草持有 8873 亿日元（56 亿美元）现金及现金等价物，奥驰亚则持有 27 亿美元。BTIG 的 Bennett 补充称，日本烟草还可通过重新发行未注销库存股筹资约 74 亿美元，为交易提供资金。 日本政府持有日本烟草 37.6% 的股份。该公司十多年来也一直在非洲收购资产。 收购帝国品牌的非洲和中东业务将与其在非洲的布局相契合，并有助于弥补俄罗斯资产被没收后的收入损失——本月，俄罗斯总统 Vladimir Putin 下令没收该公司在俄资产。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 美国黑五消费“K型分化”加剧：富人越买越多，穷人勒紧裤腰带
articles.summary: 美国年度最大购物季已经拉开帷幕，但消费分化正在加剧：高收入家庭计划增加节日支出，近半数低收入家庭却准备削减开销，K型消费格局正成为今年黑色星期五的主线。 据高盛零售分析师Brooke Roach团队对约1000名消费者的调查， 年收入10万美元及以上的家庭中，50%计划增加节日消费，高于去年的44%；年收入低于5万美元的家庭中，48%预计削减支出，也高于去年的46%。分析师指出，消费乐观情绪仍集中在高收入群体，中低收入家庭则更加谨慎。 与此同时，全美零售联合会（NRF）与Prosper Insights & Analytics预计，今年感恩节购物周末将吸引1.827亿消费者，较去年下降约2%。不过，购物人数减少部分源于消费时间提前：11月初已有约60%的消费者开始节日采购，高于疫情前的56%。 黑色星期五仍是最热门购物日，亚马逊和沃尔玛领跑 尽管整体购物人数预计下降，黑色星期五仍是感恩节购物周末最受欢迎的购物日。NRF对8000名消费者的调查显示，69%的潜在购物者计划在黑色星期五消费，Cyber Monday以约36%的比例位居第二。 零售商也已提前展开促销。亚马逊在电子产品线上推出全面折扣，百思买则主打限时抢购，部分平板电视折扣高达五折。 高盛调查显示，亚马逊和沃尔玛仍是消费者节日购物的首选。亚马逊稳居榜首，市场份额较去年提升1个百分点；沃尔玛位列第二，份额同比增幅最大，达到7个百分点。 从礼品品类看，礼品卡仍最受欢迎，但份额较去年下降；服装、玩具及游戏、配饰和珠宝的受欢迎程度有所上升，鞋类、家居用品、媒体及体验类礼品则有所走弱。服装消费中，运动鞋、运动服和牛仔裤是计划增加支出的主要品类，连衣裙、手袋和职业正装则是消费者计划削减开支的主要品类。 AI工具加速渗透购物决策，年轻消费者走在前列 AI正在成为消费者节日购物的新工具。 高盛调查显示， 约58%的消费者预计今年节日季会使用AI工具寻找、评估或购买礼物，较去年增加7个百分点；32%的受访者计划提高AI工具的使用频率，较去年增加6个百分点。 年轻消费者和男性是AI购物工具的主要使用群体。随着AI逐步参与商品搜索、价格比较和购买决策，购物方式也在发生变化。 油价回落缓解部分压力，低收入家庭消费仍存隐忧 对于预算承压的低收入家庭，油价下跌提供了一定缓冲。全美普通汽油均价降至每加仑约3.67美元，较9月底的约4.50美元明显回落，有望释放部分工薪家庭的可支配收入。 但这部分节省能否转化为节日消费，仍存在不确定性。如果资金更多用于食品杂货、水电账单等日常开支，对零售销售的提振就会相对有限。 消费分化也体现在价格感知上。 高盛调查显示，绝大多数消费者仍认为今年礼品价格更贵，但中高收入群体的价格压力感知较去年有所缓解，低收入群体则进一步恶化。 与此同时，折扣和促销对购物决策的重要性依然突出，与去年基本持平。 这意味着，今年节日消费的关键不仅在于消费者是否购物，更在于不同收入群体的购买力，以及零售商能否通过折扣吸引预算有限的消费者。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 民主党准备向富人和公司加税 市场根本就没开始定价
articles.summary: 民主党赢了国会之后，未来要做的事清单很长：恢复被削减的医疗补助和食品券，续上平价医疗法案的补贴，撤掉关税。据估算，这些如果不另外找钱抵补这些开支，十年内会让赤字增加4万亿美元以上。 美国选民投票踢走共和党，是因为东西越来越贵，而民主党承诺降低生活成本——但让老百姓少掏钱，政府就得多掏钱。

articles.title: 美国空军核心云平台Cloud One遭黑客入侵，内部人士警告“事态极其严重”
articles.summary: 美国空军旗舰云基础设施Cloud One据报遭到黑客入侵，可能令大量敏感的战术与人事数据面临风险。 这是美国军方最大云平台之一首次被公开披露遭突破，事件发生在平台升级期间，暴露了国防部在将核心业务迁移至商业云过程中所积累的系统性脆弱性。多名知情人士将该入侵形容为“大事件”。 据路透上周五报道， 此次入侵是在过去一个月内的平台升级过程中被发现的。目前尚不清楚攻击者的身份，也无法确认其是否实际获取了数据。 美国空军在回应中表示，不对“特定网络与系统的安全态势、漏洞或运行状态”置评，并强调持续采取审慎措施保护空军部信息、系统与任务能力。 Cloud One于2017年推出，用于存储数据并为飞机维护、军事后勤和人事档案等应用提供计算基础设施，整合了Amazon、Microsoft、Google和Oracle的云服务。 分析人士指出，该平台一旦出现长时间中断或更深层次的失陷，可能使敏感军事数据暴露。 模糊的责任归属与升温的威胁态势 据彭博报道，过去数周内，包括FBI和NSA在内的多个政府机构，以及大型银行、Microsoft和Apple均遭遇一系列网络事件与服务中断。 美国国家情报总监Jay Clayton于11月18日向众议院国土安全委员会表示，这些事件“并非协同攻击或国家支持的攻击”。国务卿Marco Rubio亦称，没有“任何”证据显示这些中断彼此关联或由黑客造成。 但外界的判断并不一致。资深网络安全专家Rodney Gullatte Jr.在接受媒体采访时直言：“我不再沉默于这样一个事实，即现在确实正在发生一场网络攻击。” 与此同时，FBI此前警告称，一款名为ARTEX的人工智能黑客框架可让“技术能力极低”的攻击者以机器速度实施复杂的多目标入侵。 国防云化的代价与先例 Cloud One并非国防部首次在云软件上出现安全事件。2023年，一台配置错误的Microsoft Azure服务器暴露了至少1TB的军事邮件，其中包含个人信息及官员之间的对话记录。 此次事件再度凸显，将作战与后勤支撑系统集中于少数商业云供应商之上，在提升效率的同时也放大了单点失陷的后果。 对市场而言，短期影响主要集中在两个方面： 一是国防IT与云服务合同的审查可能趋严，供应商在合规与安全认证上的成本将上升； 二是网络安全的预算倾斜逻辑进一步强化，身份认证、供应链安全与AI驱动的威胁检测等领域的需求预期获得支撑。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
